rounding.notes: Applied at publication only; all intermediate arithmetic is full-precision decimal. basket_cost carries more decimal places than dated_siu so the published print is reproducible from its own published figures. siu_per_usd truncates so it never overstates the work a dollar buys.

correction_notes.note: claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-4-5 (both frontier-tier) produced zero run records for this print — every attempt across all three task classes failed with the same Anthropic API error, "Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API," a provider-side billing failure, not a quality-gate failure. Both models were reachable and qualified normally in the immediately preceding print (2026-09-07). This print's basket_costs and exchange_rate_table did not disclose this exclusion with a gap row when first published, because the print pipeline (packages/print/src/cli/load-inputs.ts) silently dropped zero-run-record models before the existing excluded_reason mechanism could apply to them — fixed for every print from this one onward. The published $0.0049 figure is the correct equal-weighted average of the seven constituents that did produce real data; it is not a market move. The apparent 33% drop from 2026-09-07's $0.0073 is a mechanical consequence of losing the two most expensive constituents to a provider outage, not a change in inference cost. This incident also exposed a gap in gate design, not only disclosure: MINIMUM_QUALIFYING_MODELS gated this print's overall qualifying count (7 of 9) but not its tier composition, so it published while frontier collapsed to 3 of its 5 registered constituents — below the same minimum Frontier SIU's own standalone gate correctly applied that same day (Frontier SIU declined to publish, 3 of 5, for this exact reason). Under a per-tier version of this gate, applied retroactively for confirmation only: this print would have been refused outright, not merely disclosed after the fact. The gate now applies per-tier as well as overall for every print from this one onward — see methodology.md's Index governance for the fix.

A reasoning-token cost gap affected this print: gemini-3.1-pro-preview's reasoning tokens (RunRecord.usage.reasoning — real, captured in every run record for this print) were not priced. packages/print/src/compute/class-cost.ts computed cost from usage.output alone. Reasoning tokens are billed by the provider at the output rate — confirmed live, 2026-09-08: Google's own published pricing states "Output price (including thinking tokens)", and a separate live check (xAI's real per-call billed cost) independently confirmed the same billing convention for reasoning models generally. This is not a methodology refinement — the index measures realised cost from executed runs, and the run records already carried this field. Corrected figures, computed from this print's own real run records and price snapshot with the fix applied, not from new data: this print's dated_siu was originally reported as $0.0049; the corrected figure is $0.0060. gemini-3.1-pro-preview's own basket cost was originally reported as $0.013990; the corrected figure is $0.021777. This print itself is not recomputed or replaced — the original stands, per the revision policy's unconditional never-edit guarantee. The fix (packages/print/src/compute/class-cost.ts, cost-of-production.ts) applies forward from the next published print onward, which will show a real, one-time jump in gemini-3.1-pro-preview's cost for this methodological reason, not a market move — see docs/methodology.md's Index governance.

The reasoning-token pricing fix's effect, anticipated in this print's own correction note above, became visible in the very next print (2026-09-09): gemini-3.1-pro-preview's real basket cost, computed under the fixed formula against that day's own run records and price snapshot, was $0.020406 — close to, but not identical to, this note's own $0.021777 same-day estimate. The difference is real day-over-day price movement (a new price snapshot), not measurement error; both figures are correct for the day they describe. The full three-print picture, stated plainly: 2026-09-07's $0.0073, this print's $0.0049, and 2026-09-09's $0.0089 are each fully explained by an infrastructure failure (the Anthropic billing outage disclosed above), a pricing bug fix (this note's own subject), or a registry composition change (claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-4-5 recovering, grok-4.6 being admitted) — none of it is a change in the underlying market price of inference, and the series does not yet show a usable market trend. A live-computed, ongoing version of this comparison — splitting any future print's move into a compositional share (admitted/removed constituents) and a continuous share (movement among constituents present in both prints) — now renders on every print with a registry change; see docs/methodology.md's Registry inclusion policy.

This print includes gemini-3.1-pro-preview, whose Google Cloud billing predates the point where it was isolated to this project alone. Before that, a real, unexplained cost gap was found between Google's actual billed Gemini cost and this project's own computed cost on every day independently checked (2026-09-08 through 2026-09-10 -- 2026-09-08 far larger than the others, but the gap wasn't confined to that one day). This project's own per-token pricing was independently verified against Google's real published rates and confirmed correct, ruling out a calculation error on this project's side -- but the cause of the gap itself was never established, and Gemini's own real invoice cost for any day before isolation cannot be attributed to this project with confidence. Because that evidence gap cannot be reconstructed after the fact, this print will remain status: "provisional" permanently, not through neglect. See docs/methodology.md's Index governance (§7) for the general policy and the isolation fix that resolves this for prints going forward.
